title: ESGO/ISUOG/IOTA/ESGE Consensus Statement on the preoperative diagnosis of ovarian tumors
organization: ESGO, ISUOG, IOTA, ESGE Joint Task Force
publication_journal: Ultrasound in Obstetrics & Gynecology / Int J Gynecol Cancer
evidence_level: Tier-1 International Clinical Practice Guideline (18 Consensus Statements)
target_population: Patients with suspected ovarian / adnexal malignancy undergoing preoperative surgical planning.
key_recommendations: Transvaginal ultrasound performed by an experienced examiner or utilizing validated IOTA prediction models (ADNEX, Simple Rules Risk Model) is the primary first-line imaging modality.
Pattern recognition by expert ultrasound examiners achieves superior diagnostic accuracy (AUC ~0.94-0.96) compared to serum CA-125 or Risk of Malignancy Index (RMI).
IOTA ADNEX model is recommended to differentiate between benign, borderline, stage I primary invasive, stage II-IV primary invasive, and metastatic ovarian tumors.
Secondary imaging with pelvic dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI (or O-RADS MRI) is recommended when transvaginal ultrasound is inconclusive (O-RADS 3 or 4 with indeterminate solid tissue).
Routine use of serum CA-125 alone to diagnose benign vs malignant masses in premenopausal women is discouraged due to low specificity in endometriosis, fibroids, and pelvic infection.
